preamble: An open vowel that raises step by step and ends up as a front diphthong [eɪ]. The standard case is the English Great Vowel Shift: Middle English long /aː/ (in name, make, mate) was raised to [æː] around 1550, to [ɛː] after 1600, then to [eː], and this monophthong became the diphthong [eɪ] in Standard English in the 18th century or later. Scots raised /aː/ only to monophthongal [eː]. No clear second case from another language has been found, so the change is treated as rare.

examples.note: Great Vowel Shift: /aː/ passed through [æː], [ɛː] and [eː] before diphthongizing to [eɪ] in the 18th century or later.
During the 16th–17th centuries this vowel merged with the diphthong of vain and vein (pane–pain merger), and the merged vowel later became [eɪ].

sources: Wikipedia (2026). Phonological history of English diphthongs. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phonological_history_of_English_diphthongs
